```{r constants}
COL_NOEXP  <- "#999999"
COL_ERRMON <- "#D97B3A"
COL_PASSIV <- "#3A7FBF"

GROUP_COLORS <- c("No-exposure" = COL_NOEXP,
                  "Error-monitoring" = COL_ERRMON,
                  "Passive-listening" = COL_PASSIV)
GROUP_ORDER  <- c("No-exposure", "Error-monitoring", "Passive-listening")
GROUP_PREFIX <- c("No-exposure" = "ne",
                  "Error-monitoring" = "em",
                  "Passive-listening" = "pl")

# Manual Cohen's d
# d = 0.2 is small, 0.5 is medium, 0.8 is large.
compute_cohens_d <- function(x, y) {
  nx <- length(x); ny <- length(y)
  if (nx < 2 || ny < 2) return(NA_real_)
  pooled_sd <- sqrt(((nx - 1) * var(x) + (ny - 1) * var(y)) / (nx + ny - 2))
  if (pooled_sd == 0) return(NA_real_)
  (mean(x) - mean(y)) / pooled_sd
}

# Reusable pie chart
make_pie <- function(df, col, title = "", palette = "Set2") {
  d <- df %>%
    count(!!sym(col)) %>%
    mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n)),
           label = paste0(!!sym(col), "\n(", n, ", ", pct, "%)"))
  ggplot(d, aes(x = "", y = n, fill = !!sym(col))) +
    geom_col(width = 1, alpha = 0.9) +
    coord_polar("y") +
    geom_text(aes(label = label), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 3.2) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = palette) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    labs(title = title)
}

# Standardize state names for the US map.
# Handles full names (any case), abbreviations, and known zip codes.
clean_state <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(x)
  x_lower <- tolower(x)
  idx <- match(x_lower, tolower(state.name))
  if (!is.na(idx)) return(tolower(state.name[idx]))
  idx <- match(toupper(x), state.abb)
  if (!is.na(idx)) return(tolower(state.name[idx]))
  # Zip code fallback: first digit → region (approximate)
  if (grepl("^\\d{5}$", x)) {
    zip_state <- c("0"="massachusetts","1"="new york","2"="virginia",
                   "3"="georgia","4"="kentucky","5"="minnesota",
                   "6"="kansas","7"="texas","8"="colorado","9"="california")
    first <- substr(x, 1, 1)
    if (first %in% names(zip_state)) return(zip_state[[first]])
  }
  NA_character_
}

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(
  plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
  plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "grey40"),
  axis.title    = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.line     = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3),
  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
  legend.position = "top"
))
```


# 0. Data Loading and Participant Exclusion

## 0.1 Load raw data

```{r load-raw}
raw_folder <- "../data/follow-up-no-error"
raw_files  <- list.files(raw_folder, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
stopifnot("No CSVs found in follow-up-no-error folder." = length(raw_files) > 0)

# na = "" means only truly empty cells become NA. The default also converts
# the literal string "NA" to missing, but participants sometimes type "NA"
# as a real response (meaning "I couldn't understand this sentence").
df_raw <- map_dfr(raw_files, ~read_csv(.x, show_col_types = FALSE, na = ""))
all_pids <- unique(df_raw$participant_id)
cat(sprintf("Loaded %d file(s): %s\nTotal rows: %d, Total participants: %d\n",
            length(raw_files), paste(basename(raw_files), collapse = ", "),
            nrow(df_raw), length(all_pids)))
```

## 0.2 Exclusion pipeline

We exclude participants for three reasons, applied in order:

1. **Screened out by FindingFive**: failed the headphone check (3 attempts) or the comprehension quiz. These participants hit the Exit block.
2. **Non-English native language**: anyone who did not select English as their only native language. This study requires monolingual English speakers because bilingual listeners (especially Spanish--English) may have different adaptation patterns.
3. **Failed attention check**: must answer at least 3 of 4 no-error attention check filler trials correctly (fill_25--fill_28).

```{r exclusion}
# Step 1: Screened-out participants
# They hit Exit (headphone fail) or Exit_SanityCheck (comprehension fail).
screened_out <- df_raw %>%
  filter(block_name %in% c("Exit_SanityCheck", "Exit",
                            "Ineligible_Prolific_confirmation_code")) %>%
  distinct(participant_id) %>%
  pull(participant_id)

# Also check the branching columns for safety
screened_branch <- df_raw %>%
  filter(branch_eligiblenotEligible == "notEligible" |
         branch_sanitycheckFailsanitycheckPass == "sanitycheckFail") %>%
  distinct(participant_id) %>%
  pull(participant_id)

screened_out <- unique(c(screened_out, screened_branch))

cat(sprintf("Step 1 — Screened out by FindingFive: %d\n", length(screened_out)))

# Step 2: Native language check (among non-screened participants)
remaining <- setdiff(all_pids, screened_out)

lang_check <- df_raw %>%
  filter(participant_id %in% remaining,
         response_name == "native_language") %>%
  select(participant_id, native_language = response_value) %>%
  mutate(english_only = grepl("^\\['English'\\]$", native_language))

non_english_ids <- lang_check %>% filter(!english_only) %>% pull(participant_id)

if (length(non_english_ids) > 0) {
  cat(sprintf("Step 2 — Non-English native language: %d\n", length(non_english_ids)))
  lang_check %>% filter(!english_only) %>% knitr::kable()
} else {
  cat("Step 2 — Non-English native language: 0\n")
}

remaining <- setdiff(remaining, non_english_ids)

# Step 3: Attention checks (3/4 no-error filler trials)
att_key <- tibble(
  stim = c("fill_25_new", "fill_26_new", "fill_27_new", "fill_28_new"),
  question = c("How many legs does a dog have?",
               "What state is Los Angeles in?",
               "What day comes after Monday?",
               "What color is a school bus?"),
  pattern = c("\\b(four|4)\\b", "california", "tuesday", "yellow")
)

att_data <- df_raw %>%
  filter(grepl("^Trivia_List", block_name),
         response_name == "Trivia_Text_Response",
         stimuli_presented %in% att_key$stim,
         participant_id %in% remaining) %>%
  select(participant_id, stimuli_presented, response_value) %>%
  left_join(att_key, by = c("stimuli_presented" = "stim")) %>%
  mutate(answer = tolower(trimws(response_value)),
         correct = mapply(function(a, p) grepl(p, a, ignore.case = TRUE),
                          answer, pattern))

att_scores <- att_data %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  summarise(correct = sum(correct), total = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(pass = correct >= 3)

att_fail_ids <- att_scores %>% filter(!pass) %>% pull(participant_id)

cat(sprintf("Step 3 — Failed attention check (<3/4): %d\n", length(att_fail_ids)))
if (length(att_fail_ids) > 0) {
  att_scores %>% filter(!pass) %>% knitr::kable()
}

remaining <- setdiff(remaining, att_fail_ids)

# Final included sample
included_ids <- remaining
df_incl <- df_raw %>% filter(participant_id %in% included_ids)

cat(sprintf("\nExclusion summary\n"))
cat(sprintf("Total recruited:            %d\n", length(all_pids)))
cat(sprintf("Screened out (FindingFive): -%d\n", length(screened_out)))
cat(sprintf("Non-English native lang:   -%d\n", length(non_english_ids)))
cat(sprintf("Failed attention check:    -%d\n", length(att_fail_ids)))
cat(sprintf("Included in analysis:       %d\n", length(included_ids)))
```

## 0.3 Assign participant IDs

We assign short IDs (pl-1, pl-2, ...) only to included participants.

```{r assign-pids}
pid_map_pl <- df_incl %>%
  distinct(participant_id) %>%
  arrange(participant_id) %>%
  mutate(pid = paste0("pl-", row_number()))

df_incl <- df_incl %>%
  left_join(pid_map_pl, by = "participant_id")

cat(sprintf("Assigned IDs pl-1 through pl-%d\n", nrow(pid_map_pl)))
```

All summaries in this section are for the included passive-listening participants only. Demographics for the No-exposure and Error-monitoring groups are reported in main-analysis-improved.Rmd.

## 1.1 Completion time

```{r completion-time, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
dur <- df_incl %>%
  distinct(participant_id, pid, participation_duration) %>%
  mutate(minutes = as.numeric(participation_duration) / 60)

dur_mean <- mean(dur$minutes)
dur_sd   <- sd(dur$minutes)

ggplot(dur, aes(x = minutes)) +
  geom_density(fill = COL_PASSIV, alpha = 0.35, color = COL_PASSIV) +
  geom_rug(alpha = 0.5, color = COL_PASSIV) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = dur_mean, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
  annotate("text", x = dur_mean + 1, y = Inf, vjust = 2, hjust = 0, size = 3.5,
           label = sprintf("M = %.1f min\nSD = %.1f min", dur_mean, dur_sd)) +
  labs(title = "Study Completion Time (Included Participants)",
       x = "Minutes", y = "Density")

cat(sprintf("Completion time: M = %.1f, SD = %.1f, range = %.0f-%.0f min\n",
            dur_mean, dur_sd, min(dur$minutes), max(dur$minutes)))
```

Participants rated two items on a 1--5 scale: 1 = Never, 2 = Sometimes, 3 = Half the time, 4 = Often, 5 = All the time.

```{r exposure, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}

exposure <- quest %>%
  filter(response_name %in% c("exposure_spanish", "exposure_spanish_accent")) %>%

exposure %>%
  mutate(rating_num = as.integer(as.character(rating))) %>%
```

# 2. Data Quality Checks

All checks below are for the included participants only.

## 2.1 Block completeness

```{r block-completeness}
# Every included participant should have all core blocks.
expected_blocks <- c("Welcome", "Headphone_check", "Begin", "Prac_Trivia",
                     "Pre_Main_Trivia_Quiz", "Transcription", "Questionnaire")

block_check <- df_incl %>%
  group_by(pid) %>%
  summarise(blocks = list(unique(block_name)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(has_all = sapply(blocks, function(b) all(expected_blocks %in% b)))

if (all(block_check$has_all)) {
  cat(sprintf("PASS: All %d included participants completed every core block.\n",
              nrow(block_check)))
} else {
  missing <- block_check %>% filter(!has_all)
  cat(sprintf("FAIL: %d participant(s) are missing blocks:\n", nrow(missing)))
  missing %>% select(pid) %>% knitr::kable()
}
```

## 2.2 Trial counts

```{r trial-counts}
trivia <- df_incl %>%
  filter(grepl("^Trivia_List", block_name),
         response_name == "Trivia_Choice_Response") %>%
  mutate(item_type = case_when(
    grepl("^targ_", stimuli_presented) ~ "target",
    grepl("^fill_", stimuli_presented) ~ "filler",
    TRUE ~ "unknown"))

# Check total trial count per participant (should be 56)
trial_totals <- trivia %>% count(pid, name = "total_trials")
all_56 <- all(trial_totals$total_trials == 56)
cat(sprintf("Total trivia trials: %s (all %d have 56)\n",
            if (all_56) "PASS" else "FAIL", nrow(trial_totals)))

# Check target/filler split (should be 24 / 32)
type_counts <- trivia %>% count(pid, item_type) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = item_type, values_from = n)
all_split <- all(type_counts$target == 24 & type_counts$filler == 32)
cat(sprintf("Target/filler split (24/32): %s\n", if (all_split) "PASS" else "FAIL"))

# Check conditions within targets (should be 6 per condition A-D)
cond_counts <- trivia %>%
  filter(item_type == "target") %>%
  mutate(condition = str_extract(stimuli_presented, "(?<=targ_\\d{2}_)[A-D]")) %>%
  count(pid, condition) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = n)
all_6 <- all(cond_counts %>% select(A:D) %>% sapply(function(x) all(x == 6)))
cat(sprintf("6 targets per condition: %s\n", if (all_6) "PASS" else "FAIL"))

# Transcription count (should be 20)
trans_raw <- df_incl %>%
  filter(block_name == "Transcription", response_name == "Transcription_Response")
trans_counts <- trans_raw %>% count(pid, name = "sentences")
all_20 <- all(trans_counts$sentences == 20)
cat(sprintf("Transcription sentences (20): %s\n", if (all_20) "PASS" else "FAIL"))

# Any empty or junk transcriptions?
# With na="" in read_csv, truly empty cells are NA; "NA" typed stays as a string.
n_truly_empty <- sum(is.na(trans_raw$response_value) | trans_raw$response_value == "")
n_typed_na    <- sum(tolower(trimws(trans_raw$response_value)) %in% c("na", "n/a") &
                     !is.na(trans_raw$response_value))
cat(sprintf("Truly empty responses: %d\n", n_truly_empty))
cat(sprintf("Typed 'NA' (couldn't understand): %d\n", n_typed_na))
```

## 2.3 Counterbalancing

The 24 target items come in 4 condition versions (A/B/C/D). Each Latin Square group hears a different rotation of conditions, so each participant hears 6 targets in condition A, 6 in B, 6 in C, and 6 in D. The groups map to trivia stimulus lists: Group_1 → Trivia_List1, Group_2 → Trivia_List2, Group_3 → Trivia_List3, Group_4 → Trivia_List4.

```{r counterbalancing}
participants <- df_incl %>% distinct(participant_id, pid, group_id)
group_counts <- participants %>% count(group_id, name = "n")

cat("Group distribution:\n")
group_counts %>% knitr::kable()

if (nrow(participants) >= 8) {
  chi <- chisq.test(group_counts$n)
  cat(sprintf("\nChi-square test for equal distribution: X2 = %.2f, p = %.3f\n",
              chi$statistic, chi$p.value))
  cat(if (chi$p.value > .05) "PASS: no evidence of imbalance\n"
      else "WARNING: groups may be unbalanced\n")
}
```

## 2.4 Trivia response times

The RT is recorded from the moment the audio finishes playing. Trials with RT < 200ms are implausibly fast (the participant could not have processed the question that quickly) and are excluded from this plot.

```{r trivia-rt, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
trivia_rt <- df_incl %>%
  filter(grepl("^Trivia_List", block_name),
         response_name == "Trivia_Choice_Response") %>%
  mutate(rt_ms = as.numeric(response_rt))

n_under_200 <- sum(trivia_rt$rt_ms < 200, na.rm = TRUE)
pct_under_200 <- round(100 * n_under_200 / nrow(trivia_rt), 1)
cat(sprintf("Trials with RT < 200ms: %d / %d (%.1f%%)\n", n_under_200, nrow(trivia_rt), pct_under_200))

trivia_rt_clean <- trivia_rt %>% filter(rt_ms >= 200)

ggplot(trivia_rt_clean, aes(x = rt_ms / 1000)) +
  geom_density(fill = COL_PASSIV, alpha = 0.35, color = COL_PASSIV) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = Inf, vjust = 2, hjust = -0.1,
           label = "500ms", size = 3, color = "grey50") +
  labs(title = "Trivia Choice Response Time (excluding RT < 200ms)",
       x = "Response time (seconds)", y = "Density") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, NA))

# The RT distribution has a long right tail (some participants take 30+ seconds
# on a trial, likely due to distraction or tabbing away). The median is a much
# better summary than the mean for skewed distributions.
q <- quantile(trivia_rt_clean$rt_ms, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("RT after excluding <200ms: Median = %.0f ms, IQR = [%.0f, %.0f] ms\n",
            q[2], q[1], q[3]))
cat(sprintf("Trials > 10s: %d (%.1f%%) — likely distraction, not response time\n",
            sum(trivia_rt_clean$rt_ms > 10000, na.rm = TRUE),
            100 * mean(trivia_rt_clean$rt_ms > 10000, na.rm = TRUE)))
```


# 3. Keyword Scoring and Data Loading

## 3.1 How keyword scoring works

Each transcription sentence has a list of keywords (content words that carry meaning). Scoring compares what the participant typed against these keywords using partial matching (R's `pmatch`).

`pmatch` checks whether a keyword is a **prefix** of any word in the transcription. So "notice" matches "noticed" (prefix), but "weight" does not match "wait" (different letters). A keyword only counts once.

| Example | |
|:---|:---|
| Keywords | noticed, weight, lead |
| Typed | "He noticed the wait of the led" |
| noticed → "noticed" | match (1 point) |
| weight → "wait" | no match (0) |
| lead → "led" | no match (0) |
| Score | 1 / 3 = 33.3% |

```{r scoring-key}
key.df <- read.delim("../data/transcription_scoring.txt", header = TRUE, sep = ",") %>%
  mutate(Sentence = as.character(Sentence))

cat(sprintf("Scoring key: %d sentences, %d total keywords\n",
            nrow(key.df), sum(as.numeric(key.df$NumKeywords))))
```

```{r scoring-function}
# Identical to main-analysis-improved.Rmd. Must stay the same.
num.keywords.correct <- function(transcription, keywords) {
  keys  <- gsub("[[:punct:]]", "", tolower(as.character(keywords)))
  trans <- gsub("[[:punct:]]", "", tolower(as.character(transcription)))
  key_words   <- unlist(strsplit(keys, " "))
  trans_words <- unlist(strsplit(trans, " "))
  sum(!is.na(pmatch(key_words, trans_words)))
}
```

## 3.2 Load all three groups

```{r load-groups}
load_transcription_group <- function(folder_path, group_label) {
  files <- list.files(folder_path, pattern = "_transcription_data\\.csv$",
                      full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)
  if (length(files) == 0) {
    files <- list.files(folder_path, pattern = "transcription_data\\.csv$",
                        full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)
    files <- files[1]
  }
  if (length(files) == 0 || is.na(files[1])) {
    warning(paste("No data found for", group_label))
    return(NULL)
  }
  # Load and combine ALL matching files (e.g., main batch + test run)
  map_dfr(files, ~read_csv(.x, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
            mutate(across(everything(), as.character))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(stimulus_files_presented),
           stimulus_files_presented != "",
           block == "Transcription") %>%
    mutate(Filename = basename(stimulus_files_presented),
           Transcription = response_value,
           group = group_label)
}

df_noexp  <- load_transcription_group("../data/baseline_and_error_detection/preprocessed/transcrip_baseline", "No-exposure")
df_errmon <- load_transcription_group("../data/baseline_and_error_detection/preprocessed/main_batch3", "Error-monitoring")

# Passive-listening: from the included participants' raw data
df_passiv <- df_incl %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.character)) %>%
  filter(block_name == "Transcription",
         response_name == "Transcription_Response",
         !is.na(stimulus_files_presented),
         stimulus_files_presented != "") %>%
  mutate(Filename = basename(stimulus_files_presented),
         Transcription = response_value,
         group = "Passive-listening")

df_all_raw <- bind_rows(df_noexp, df_errmon, df_passiv)
cat(sprintf("Combined: %d total transcription rows\n", nrow(df_all_raw)))
```

## 3.3 Score and filter

```{r score-and-filter}
df_all <- df_all_raw %>%
  inner_join(key.df %>% select(-SentenceSet), by = c("Filename" = "Sentence"))

clean_transcription <- function(x) {
  x <- tolower(as.character(x))
  for (pat in c("&lt&","&gt&","&quot&","&comma&","&semicol&","&pipe&","&apos&")) {
    rep <- c("<",">","\"",",",";","|","'")[match(pat,
           c("&lt&","&gt&","&quot&","&comma&","&semicol&","&pipe&","&apos&"))]
    x <- gsub(pat, rep, x, fixed = TRUE)
  }
  x
}

df_all <- df_all %>%
  mutate(
    Transcription = clean_transcription(Transcription),
    NumKeywordsCorrect = mapply(num.keywords.correct, Transcription, Keywords),
    PropKeywordsCorrect = as.numeric(NumKeywordsCorrect) / as.numeric(NumKeywords)
  )

# Error-monitoring attention check filter (6/8 error detection threshold).
eligible_ids_file <- "../data/baseline_and_error_detection/preprocessed/main_batch3/eligible_participant_ids.csv"
if (file.exists(eligible_ids_file)) {
  eligible_ids <- read_csv(eligible_ids_file, show_col_types = FALSE)$participant_id
  n_before <- n_distinct(df_all$participant_id[df_all$group == "Error-monitoring"])
  df_all <- df_all %>%
    filter(group != "Error-monitoring" | participant_id %in% eligible_ids)
  n_after <- n_distinct(df_all$participant_id[df_all$group == "Error-monitoring"])
  cat(sprintf("Error-monitoring: %d -> %d after 6/8 error detection filter\n", n_before, n_after))
}

# --- Merge trial durations for fatigue analysis (Section 5.5) ---
# No trials are excluded; durations are used for the fatigue check only.
get_trial_durations <- function(raw_df, group_label) {
  raw_df %>%
    filter(block_name == "Transcription",
           !is.na(stimulus_files_presented),
           stimulus_files_presented != "") %>%
    mutate(Filename = basename(as.character(stimulus_files_presented)),
           trial_duration_sec = as.numeric(trial_duration) / 1000) %>%
    filter(!is.na(trial_duration_sec), trial_duration_sec > 0) %>%
    select(participant_id, Filename, trial_duration_sec) %>%
    distinct()
}

em_raw <- bind_rows(
  read_csv("../data/baseline_and_error_detection/raw/main_120325_48subj.csv",
           show_col_types = FALSE),
  read_csv("../data/baseline_and_error_detection/raw/main_112825_test_run_4subj.csv",
           show_col_types = FALSE)
)
ne_raw1 <- read_csv("../data/baseline_and_error_detection/raw/transcription_baseline_batch1_14subj.csv",
                     show_col_types = FALSE)
ne_raw2 <- read_csv("../data/baseline_and_error_detection/raw/transcription_baseline_batch2_10subj.csv",
                     show_col_types = FALSE)

dur_em <- get_trial_durations(em_raw, "Error-monitoring")
dur_ne <- bind_rows(get_trial_durations(ne_raw1, "No-exposure"),
                     get_trial_durations(ne_raw2, "No-exposure"))
dur_pl <- get_trial_durations(df_raw, "Passive-listening")
dur_all <- bind_rows(dur_em, dur_ne, dur_pl)

df_all <- df_all %>%
  left_join(dur_all, by = c("participant_id", "Filename"))

df_all <- df_all %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = GROUP_ORDER))

# Assign easy-to-read IDs.
# Passive-listening: use the IDs from Section 0.3 so they match.
# No-exposure and Error-monitoring: assign new sequential IDs.
df_all <- df_all %>%
  left_join(pid_map_pl %>% select(participant_id, pid_from_sec0 = pid),
            by = "participant_id") %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  mutate(pid_num = dense_rank(participant_id)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(pid = case_when(
    group == "Passive-listening" & !is.na(pid_from_sec0) ~ pid_from_sec0,
    TRUE ~ paste0(GROUP_PREFIX[as.character(group)], "-", pid_num)
  )) %>%
  select(-pid_from_sec0)

df_all <- df_all %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  mutate(trial_order = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

df_all %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(N = n_distinct(participant_id),
            Trials = n(),
            Mean = mean(PropKeywordsCorrect, na.rm = TRUE),
            SD = sd(PropKeywordsCorrect, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Transcription accuracy by group")
```


# 4. Research Questions

Our core question: does concurrent error monitoring block accent adaptation?

| Group | During trivia | During transcription | Tests |
|:------|:-------------|:--------------------|:------|
| No-exposure | No trivia | Transcribe in noise | No prior exposure |
| Error-monitoring | Listen + answer + detect errors | Transcribe in noise | Adaptation with divided attention |
| Passive-listening | Listen + answer only | Transcribe in noise | Adaptation with full attention |

Hypotheses:

- H1 (Monitoring blocks): Passive-listening > Error-monitoring > No-exposure
- H2 (Independent): Passive-listening = Error-monitoring > No-exposure
- H3 (No adaptation): All groups equal


# 5. Visualizations and Analysis

## 5.1 Figure 1: Group comparison

Error bars are 95% bootstrapped CIs (2000 resamples). A bootstrap CI resamples the data with replacement, computes the mean each time, and takes the middle 95% of those means. If two groups' CIs do not overlap, their means likely differ.

```{r fig1-groups, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
pts <- df_all %>%
  group_by(group, pid) %>%
  summarise(M = mean(PropKeywordsCorrect, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

summ <- df_all %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(stats = list(smean.cl.boot(PropKeywordsCorrect, B = 2000)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  unnest_wider(stats)

# Raincloud-style plot: violin (distribution shape) + jittered points + mean/CI
ggplot(pts, aes(x = group, y = M, color = group, fill = group)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.15, color = NA, width = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.08, alpha = 0.45, size = 1.8) +
  geom_pointrange(data = summ, aes(y = Mean, ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper),
                  color = "black", size = 0.5, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_text(data = summ, aes(y = Mean, label = percent(Mean, accuracy = 0.1)),
            color = "black", hjust = -0.4, size = 3.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = GROUP_COLORS) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = GROUP_COLORS) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Transcription Accuracy by Group",
       subtitle = "Violin = distribution, dots = individuals, black = mean with 95% bootstrap CI",
       y = "Keyword Accuracy", x = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

### Distribution overlay

The overlapping density curves make it easy to see how much the three groups' distributions overlap — especially PL vs. EM.

```{r fig2-learning, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
learning <- df_all %>%

            .groups = "drop") %>%

for (grp in levels(df_all$group)) {

}
```

## 5.3 Figure 3: Adaptation benefit over No-exposure

For each exposure group, we compute how much better they did compared to No-exposure. If a bar's CI does not cross zero, that group benefited from exposure. Comparing the two bars shows whether monitoring mattered.

```{r fig3-benefit, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
df_agg <- df_all %>%
  group_by(pid, group) %>%
  summarise(acc = mean(PropKeywordsCorrect, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(group = droplevels(group), acc = as.numeric(acc))

baseline_m <- mean(df_agg$acc[df_agg$group == "No-exposure"])

set.seed(123)
benefit_plot <- df_agg %>%
  filter(group != "No-exposure") %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(stats = list(smean.cl.boot(acc, B = 2000)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  unnest_wider(stats) %>%
  mutate(benefit = Mean - baseline_m,
         ci_lo = Lower - baseline_m, ci_hi = Upper - baseline_m)

ggplot(benefit_plot, aes(x = group, y = benefit, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.45, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lo, ymax = ci_hi), width = 0.06, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%+.1f pp", benefit * 100)), vjust = -1.2, size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = GROUP_COLORS) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(min(benefit_plot$ci_lo, -0.03) - 0.02,
                            max(benefit_plot$ci_hi, 0.03) + 0.04)) +
  labs(title = "Adaptation Benefit Over No-exposure",
       subtitle = "Bar = group mean minus No-exposure mean, error bars = 95% bootstrap CI",
       y = "Benefit (pp)", x = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

cat("Bootstrap CI test (does the CI exclude zero?):\n")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(benefit_plot))) {
  r <- benefit_plot[i, ]
  sig <- !(r$ci_lo <= 0 & r$ci_hi >= 0)
  cat(sprintf("  %s: %+.1f pp [%.1f, %.1f] %s\n",
              r$group, r$benefit * 100, r$ci_lo * 100, r$ci_hi * 100,
              if (sig) "significant" else "not significant"))
}
```


## 5.4 Linear Mixed-Effects Model (LMM)

### Why an LMM?

Each participant contributes 20 data points (one per sentence), and each sentence is heard by multiple participants. A simple t-test would treat every row as independent, inflating the sample size. The LMM accounts for this by estimating how much variation comes from individual
differences between people (random intercept for participant) and differences between sentences (random intercept for sentence).

### Treatment coding

Treatment coding converts the three-level group variable into two dummy variables using 0s and 1s. The reference group (No-exposure) gets 0 on both dummies. Each other group gets 1 on one dummy and 0 on the other:

|  | Dummy 1 (EM) | Dummy 2 (PL) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| No-exposure (reference) | 0 | 0 |
| Error-monitoring | 1 | 0 |
| Passive-listening | 0 | 1 |

The intercept equals the reference group's mean (No-exposure). Each coefficient is the difference between that group and the reference. R sets this up automatically with `relevel()`.

This differs from sum coding (which uses -0.5 and +0.5 and puts the grand mean in the intercept). We use treatment coding because the reference group (No-exposure) is the natural baseline, and we want each coefficient to directly answer "did this group adapt?"

This gives us two coefficients:

- **$\beta_{PL}$ (Passive-listening)**: How much better Passive-listening performed compared to No-exposure. This is the adaptation benefit from passive listening.
- **$\beta_{EM}$ (Error-monitoring)**: How much better Error-monitoring performed compared to No-exposure. This is the adaptation benefit from listening with error monitoring.

If $\beta_{PL}$ is significant but $\beta_{EM}$ is not, it suggests monitoring blocked adaptation.

As a follow-up, we refit the model with Error-monitoring as the reference to directly test whether $\beta_{PL}$ differs from $\beta_{EM}$.

| $\beta_{PL}$ (PL vs NE) | $\beta_{EM}$ (EM vs NE) | PL vs EM | Conclusion |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| sig | not sig | -- | Monitoring blocks adaptation (H1) |
| sig | sig, smaller | sig | Monitoring partially reduces adaptation |
| sig | sig, same size | n.s. | Monitoring does not interfere (H2) |
| not sig | not sig | -- | No adaptation from exposure (H3) |

```{r lmm-treatment}
df_lmm <- df_all %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = GROUP_ORDER),
         participant_id = factor(participant_id),
         Filename = factor(Filename))

# Treatment coding: No-exposure is the reference.
# R's default contrasts for unordered factors is contr.treatment,
# so releveling to put No-exposure first sets it as the reference.
df_lmm$group <- relevel(df_lmm$group, ref = "No-exposure")

lmm_fit <- lmer(
  PropKeywordsCorrect ~ group + (1 | participant_id) + (1 | Filename),
  data = df_lmm)

model_summ <- summary(lmm_fit)
print(model_summ)

fe <- fixef(lmm_fit)
cat(sprintf("\nNo-exposure mean (intercept): %.1f%%\n", 100 * fe["(Intercept)"]))

# β_EM: Error-monitoring benefit over No-exposure
em_est <- fe["groupError-monitoring"]
em_p   <- model_summ$coefficients["groupError-monitoring", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat(sprintf("\nβ_EM (Error-monitoring - No-exposure): %+.1f pp, p = %.4f", em_est * 100, em_p))
cat(if (em_p < .05) " -> significant, error monitoring led to adaptation\n"
    else " -> not significant, no evidence of adaptation with monitoring\n")

# β_PL: Passive-listening benefit over No-exposure
pl_est <- fe["groupPassive-listening"]
pl_p   <- model_summ$coefficients["groupPassive-listening", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat(sprintf("β_PL (Passive-listening - No-exposure): %+.1f pp, p = %.4f", pl_est * 100, pl_p))
cat(if (pl_p < .05) " -> significant, passive listening led to adaptation\n"
    else " -> not significant\n")
```

### Follow-up: Passive-listening vs. Error-monitoring

To test whether the two exposure groups differ, we refit the same model with Error-monitoring as the reference. The Passive-listening coefficient then directly tests PL vs EM.

```{r lmm-pl-vs-em}
df_lmm_em <- df_lmm %>% mutate(group = relevel(group, ref = "Error-monitoring"))

lmm_fit_em <- lmer(
  PropKeywordsCorrect ~ group + (1 | participant_id) + (1 | Filename),
  data = df_lmm_em)

fe_em <- fixef(lmm_fit_em)
summ_em <- summary(lmm_fit_em)

pl_vs_em <- fe_em["groupPassive-listening"]
pl_vs_em_p <- summ_em$coefficients["groupPassive-listening", "Pr(>|t|)"]

cat(sprintf("PL - EM: %+.1f pp, p = %.4f", pl_vs_em * 100, pl_vs_em_p))
cat(if (pl_vs_em_p < .05) " -> significant, monitoring reduced adaptation\n"
    else " -> not significant, no evidence the two exposure groups differ\n")
```

### Figure 4: LMM coefficient forest plot

This shows the three contrasts from the LMM with 95% confidence intervals. If a CI does not cross the dashed zero line, that effect is significant.

```{r fig4-forest, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.5}
# Extract the three key contrasts and their CIs from the two models
coef_df <- tibble(
  contrast = c("Error-monitoring\nvs No-exposure",
               "Passive-listening\nvs No-exposure",
               "Passive-listening\nvs Error-monitoring"),
  estimate = c(em_est, pl_est, pl_vs_em),
  se = c(model_summ$coefficients["groupError-monitoring", "Std. Error"],
         model_summ$coefficients["groupPassive-listening", "Std. Error"],
         summ_em$coefficients["groupPassive-listening", "Std. Error"]),
  p = c(em_p, pl_p, pl_vs_em_p)
) %>%
  mutate(ci_lo = estimate - 1.96 * se,
         ci_hi = estimate + 1.96 * se,
         sig = p < .05,
         contrast = factor(contrast, levels = rev(contrast)))

ggplot(coef_df, aes(x = estimate * 100, y = contrast)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = ci_lo * 100, xmax = ci_hi * 100, color = sig),
                  size = 0.6, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%+.1f pp, p = %.3f", estimate * 100, p)),
            vjust = -1, size = 3.2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#2166AC", "FALSE" = "#999999"),
                     guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "LMM Coefficient Estimates",
       subtitle = "95% CI; blue = significant (p < .05)",
       x = "Effect size (percentage points)", y = NULL)
```

## 5.5 Accent-relevant keyword analysis

Not all keywords are equally affected by the Spanish accent. Some keywords contain phonological contrasts that are systematically altered in Spanish-accented English (e.g., /ɪ/ → /i/ as in "ship" → "sheep", /θ/ → /t/ as in "bath" → "bat"). If adaptation reaches this level, the benefit should be concentrated in these accent-relevant keywords rather
than spread evenly across all keywords.

The trivia stimuli (exposure phase) were designed to systematically include all 6 targeted contrasts, with 4 items per contrast across the 24 targets --- so each contrast appears multiple times during exposure. The transcription sentences (test phase), by contrast, were selected from a separate recording pool that also contains challenging English contrasts for Spanish speakers, but the coverage is far less exhaustive:

| Contrast | Trivia (4 items each, all minimal pairs) | Transcription keywords |
|:---------|:----------------------------------------|:----------------------|
| /ɪ/ → /i/ | will/wheel, sit/seat, knit/neat, still/steal | rip, ship, his, weep, feet, peel, ... (17 kw) |
| /ʃ/ → /s/ | clash/class, Irish/iris, rushed/rust, plush/plus (coda) | she, should (onset), issue (medial) (3 kw) |
| /k/ → /g/ | kilt/guilt, come/gum, cane/gain, cot/got | cloud, commented, consume, ... (9 kw) |
| /θ/ → /t/ | cloth/clot, path/pat, both/boat, fourth/fort | wrath, math, bath, booth, something, with (6 kw) |
| /v/ → /b/ | very/berry, vote/boat, valid/ballad, vent/bent | value, have, obvious (3 kw) |
| /ʊ/ → /u/ | could/cooed, pulls/pools, would/wooed, full/fool | full, look (2 kw) |

Key differences between the two sets:

- The trivia items are minimal pairs where the substitution changes word identity (e.g., clash → class). The transcription keywords are scored by whether participants recognize the word at all, regardless of the contrast.
- Coverage is uneven in the transcription (17 keywords for /ɪ/→/i/ but only 2 for /ʊ/→/u/), and each keyword typically appears once. In the trivia, each contrast appears at least 4 times.
- Syllable position may differ (e.g., /ʃ/→/s/ appears in coda in the trivia but onset in the transcription keywords "she" and "should").

We are not claiming to pinpoint which level adaptation reaches. Both speakers were rated as having a moderate-to-strong accent by our listeners, and transcription-in-noise is an established, robust measure of overall accent adaptation used in prior work (e.g., Bradlow & Bent, 2008). The accent-relevant keyword analysis is exploratory: it asks whether the benefit happens to concentrate on contrast-carrying words, but a global benefit is equally consistent with successful adaptation.

```{r accent-keywords-setup}

    "wrath",       "/θ/→/t/",
    "math",        "/θ/→/t/",
    "bath",        "/θ/→/t/",

    "something",   "/θ/→/t/",
    "with",        "/θ/→/t/",
    "value",       "/v/→/b/",
    "have",        "/v/→/b/",
    "obvious",     "/v/→/b/",

  ),
  tribble(

    "weep",      "/ɪ/→/i/",

    "theme",     "/ɪ/→/i/",
    "heel",      "/ɪ/→/i/",
    "bead",      "/ɪ/→/i/",
    "sloth",     "/ɪ/→/i/"
  )
)

cat(sprintf("Accent-relevant keywords: %d (across %d contrasts)\n",
            nrow(keyword_contrast), n_distinct(keyword_contrast$contrast)))
```

```{r accent-keywords-score, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
# Score each keyword individually using the same pmatch logic.
# Then tag each keyword as accent-relevant or not.
kw_results <- df_all %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    kw_list = list({
      keys <- unlist(strsplit(gsub("[[:punct:]]", "", tolower(as.character(Keywords))), " "))
      trans <- unlist(strsplit(gsub("[[:punct:]]", "", tolower(as.character(Transcription))), " "))
      tibble(
        keyword = keys,
        correct = !is.na(pmatch(keys, trans)),
        accent_relevant = keys %in% keyword_contrast$keyword
      )
    })
  ) %>%
  unnest(kw_list) %>%
  ungroup()

# Per-participant accuracy by keyword type
kw_pp <- kw_results %>%
  group_by(group, pid, accent_relevant) %>%
  summarise(accuracy = mean(correct), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(kw_type = ifelse(accent_relevant, "Accent-relevant", "Non-accent"))

# Summary table
kw_pp %>%
  group_by(group, kw_type) %>%
  summarise(M = round(mean(accuracy), 3),
            SD = round(sd(accuracy), 3),
            N = n(),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Accuracy by group and keyword type")

# Figure: accent-relevant vs non-accent by group
kw_summ <- kw_results %>%
  mutate(kw_type = ifelse(accent_relevant, "Accent-relevant", "Non-accent")) %>%
  group_by(group, kw_type) %>%
  summarise(stats = list(smean.cl.boot(as.numeric(correct), B = 2000)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  unnest_wider(stats)

ggplot(kw_summ, aes(x = group, y = Mean, fill = kw_type)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.7), width = 0.6, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper),
                position = position_dodge(0.7), width = 0.08, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(Mean, accuracy = 0.1)),
            position = position_dodge(0.7), vjust = -0.8, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Accent-relevant" = "#C75B7A", "Non-accent" = "#888888")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Accuracy by Keyword Type and Group",
       subtitle = "If adaptation is accent-specific, the group difference should be larger for accent-relevant keywords",
       y = "Keyword Accuracy", x = NULL, fill = NULL)
```

```{r accent-keywords-lmm}
# LMM: Does keyword type interact with group?
# A significant Group × Keyword Type interaction would mean the adaptation
# benefit is concentrated in accent-relevant keywords.
kw_lmm_data <- kw_results %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = GROUP_ORDER),
         kw_type = factor(ifelse(accent_relevant, "accent", "non_accent"),
                          levels = c("non_accent", "accent")),
         participant_id = factor(participant_id),
         keyword = factor(keyword))

kw_lmm_data$group <- relevel(kw_lmm_data$group, ref = "No-exposure")

kw_lmm <- glmer(
  correct ~ group * kw_type + (1 | participant_id) + (1 | keyword),
  data = kw_lmm_data, family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))

cat("GLMER: correct ~ group * kw_type + (1|participant) + (1|keyword)\n\n")
summary(kw_lmm)
```


# 5.5 Transcription Trial Duration (Fatigue Check)

To rule out fatigue as an explanation for group differences in transcription accuracy, we compared per-participant median transcription trial durations across groups. If the longer Error-monitoring session induced fatigue, EM participants might show slower trial completion.

```{r trial-duration-fatigue, fig.width=5, fig.height=3.5}
# Per-participant median trial duration (from the merged duration data)
dur_by_pid <- df_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(trial_duration_sec)) %>%
  group_by(participant_id, group) %>%
  summarise(median_dur = median(trial_duration_sec),
            mean_dur = mean(trial_duration_sec),
            n_trials = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Summary stats
dur_by_pid %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(N = n(),
            M = mean(median_dur),
            Mdn = median(median_dur),
            SD = sd(median_dur), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 1,
               caption = "Per-participant median transcription trial duration (seconds)")

# Kruskal-Wallis test (non-parametric, appropriate for skewed durations)
kw_test <- kruskal.test(median_dur ~ group, data = dur_by_pid)
cat(sprintf("\nKruskal-Wallis: H(%d) = %.2f, p = %.3f\n",
            kw_test$parameter, kw_test$statistic, kw_test$p.value))

# Violin plot
ggplot(dur_by_pid, aes(x = group, y = median_dur, fill = group)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = group), width = 0.12, alpha = 0.5, size = 2) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "crossbar", width = 0.35, color = "black",
               linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("No-exposure" = "#999999",
                                "Error-monitoring" = "#D97B3A",
                                "Passive-listening" = "#4A90D9")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("No-exposure" = "#999999",
                                 "Error-monitoring" = "#D97B3A",
                                 "Passive-listening" = "#4A90D9")) +
  labs(title = "Transcription Trial Duration by Group",
       y = "Per-participant median duration (s)", x = NULL,
       caption = sprintf("Kruskal-Wallis p = %.2f", kw_test$p.value)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        plot.caption = element_text(face = "italic"))
```


# 6. Power Analysis

### What is a power analysis?

Statistical power is the probability that a test will detect a real effect when one exists. The convention is 80% power — meaning if the true difference between PL and EM is X percentage points, we want at least an 80% chance of getting a significant p-value.

### How this simulation works

We use a simulation-based approach because our design (unequal group sizes, LMM structure) makes closed-form power formulas unreliable. For each combination of effect size and sample size, the simulation repeats 2000 times:

1. Take the **observed** Error-monitoring group data as the comparison (their real per-participant mean accuracies).
2. Simulate a hypothetical Passive-listening group of size N by drawing from a normal distribution with mean = EM mean + effect size, and SD = the pooled SD of all participant means.
3. Run a Welch t-test comparing the simulated PL group to the real EM group.
4. Count how often the test is significant at $\alpha$ = .05 and in the
   predicted direction (PL > EM).
5. Power = proportion of significant results out of 2000 simulations.

### How to read the table

- **Rows**: the true effect size in percentage points (pp). For context, the observed PL-vs-EM difference is currently about 3.8 pp.
- **Columns**: sample size N for the Passive-listening group (the EM group size is fixed at its current N).
- **Cells**: estimated power. 80% is the conventional target.
- The **dashed line** in the plot marks 80%.

### How to interpret

If the true effect is small (3 pp), even N = 50 gives only ~15% power — the study would almost always fail to detect it. At 5 pp, N = 45 gives ~55%. At 7 pp, N = 35 passes 80%.

```{r power, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
pmeans <- df_all %>%
  group_by(group, participant_id) %>%
  summarise(M = mean(PropKeywordsCorrect, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

bp_sd   <- sd(pmeans$M)
em_mean <- mean(pmeans$M[pmeans$group == "Error-monitoring"])
em_vals <- pmeans$M[pmeans$group == "Error-monitoring"]

set.seed(42)
pwr <- expand.grid(effect_pp = c(3,5,7,10,12,15),
                   n_trivia = c(30,35,40,45,50), power = NA_real_)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(pwr))) {
  eff <- pwr$effect_pp[i] / 100; n <- pwr$n_trivia[i]; sig <- 0
  for (s in 1:2000) {
    sim <- rnorm(n, mean = em_mean + eff, sd = bp_sd)
    tt <- t.test(sim, em_vals, var.equal = FALSE)
    if (tt$p.value < 0.05 && mean(sim) > em_mean) sig <- sig + 1
  }
  pwr$power[i] <- sig / 2000
}

pwr %>%
  mutate(p = sprintf("%.0f%%", power * 100)) %>%
  select(effect_pp, n_trivia, p) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = n_trivia, values_from = p, names_prefix = "N=") %>%
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Effect (pp)", "N=30","N=35","N=40","N=45","N=50"),
               caption = "Power by effect size and sample size (PL vs EM)")

ggplot(pwr, aes(x = n_trivia, y = power, color = factor(effect_pp),
                group = effect_pp)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.8, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "D", end = 0.85) +
  labs(title = "Power: Passive-listening vs Error-monitoring",
       x = "N (Passive-listening group)", y = "Power", color = "Effect (pp)")
```
